cause_quote: The commit added `signal: params.signal` only to the Gemini generateContent request in runGeminiSearch, leaving the existing `resolveCitationRedirectUrl(citation.url)` batches in the same function without the signal.
user_saw: After cancelling a Gemini web search, OpenClaw kept issuing citation redirect HEAD requests (including later batches) instead of stopping; little was directly visible beyond extra outbound traffic and delay.
summary: Forwards the Gemini search AbortSignal into the citation redirect resolver so cancelled searches stop pending and future citation HEAD requests and preserve the cancellation reason.
reasoning: Citation redirect resolution already existed in runGeminiSearch when 1143f738423 ("fix(web-search): honor provider abort signals") added cancellation support for Gemini search; that diff threaded the signal into the main request only, so cancellation never covered citation fetches from the day it was introduced. Checked the file at 1143f738423 via the contents API (citation loop present, no signal) and the commit's patch; later commits in the local history are refactors that did not touch this. It is a missed path of the cancellation feature, not a later break, hence never-worked with medium confidence.
